name: All-or-Nothing Thinking
description: Seeing things in absolute, black-and-white categories with no middle ground.
example: If I don't get this promotion, I'm a total failure.
reframeQuestion: What would a middle-ground version of this thought look like?

name: Overgeneralization
description: Taking one negative event and seeing it as a never-ending pattern.
example: I failed this quiz, I always fail everything.
reframeQuestion: Is this really 'always', or is it this one time?

name: Mental Filter
description: Dwelling on a single negative detail while ignoring the positives.
example: Focusing on one critical comment in an otherwise positive review.
reframeQuestion: What positive details am I filtering out right now?

name: Disqualifying the Positive
description: Rejecting positive experiences by insisting they 'don't count'.
example: They only complimented me to be nice.
reframeQuestion: What if the positive feedback was actually genuine?

name: Mind Reading
description: Assuming you know what others are thinking without evidence.
example: She didn't text back, she must be mad at me.
reframeQuestion: What other explanations could there be?

name: Fortune Telling
description: Predicting things will turn out badly without evidence.
example: I'm going to bomb this interview.
reframeQuestion: What evidence do I actually have for this prediction?

name: Catastrophizing
description: Expecting the worst possible outcome, or exaggerating the importance of a problem.
example: If I make a mistake at work, I'll get fired and lose everything.
reframeQuestion: What's the most realistic outcome, not just the worst one?

name: Minimization
description: Shrinking the importance of positive qualities or achievements.
example: Anyone could have done that, it's not a big deal.
reframeQuestion: Would I judge someone else's achievement this harshly?

name: Emotional Reasoning
description: Assuming that because you feel something, it must be true.
example: I feel guilty, so I must have done something wrong.
reframeQuestion: Is this a fact, or just a feeling passing through?

name: Should Statements
description: Holding rigid rules about how you or others 'should' behave.
reframeQuestion: What would I say to a friend who felt this pressure?

name: Labeling
description: Attaching a fixed, global label to yourself or others based on one event.
example: I made a mistake, I'm such an idiot.
reframeQuestion: Does one action define my whole identity?

name: Personalization
description: Blaming yourself for events not entirely under your control.
example: The project failed because of me, when it was a team effort.
reframeQuestion: What other factors contributed to this outcome?

name: Blaming
description: Holding others entirely responsible for your feelings, or yourself for theirs.
example: You made me feel this way.
reframeQuestion: What part of this reaction is within my own control?

name: Comparison Trap
description: Measuring your worth against a curated or idealized version of others.
example: Everyone else has their life together except me.
reframeQuestion: Am I comparing my behind-the-scenes to their highlight reel?

name: Negative Filtering
description: Only noticing evidence that confirms a negative belief about yourself.
example: Nobody ever checks in on me, ignoring two people who did.

name: Control Fallacies
description: Feeling either totally responsible for everything, or entirely helpless.
example: Nothing I do matters, or Everything depends on me alone.
reframeQuestion: Where does my actual influence realistically begin and end?

name: Fallacy of Fairness
description: Feeling resentful because you believe you know what's 'fair' and things don't measure up.
example: It's not fair that they got the easier task.
reframeQuestion: Is 'fairness' something I can define objectively here?

name: Heaven's Reward Fallacy
description: Expecting sacrifice and hard work to always be automatically rewarded.
example: I worked so hard, I deserve for this to work out.
reframeQuestion: Effort and outcome aren't always linked — how do I sit with that?
